subtype: Approach: repeats the same method although it is not working [Pitfall]
passage:
Saturday. Tejas here. My drawer got stuck today and my maths set was inside. I pulled. Then I pulled harder. Then I put my foot on the wall and pulled with both hands. It went bang but it did not open. My fingers hurt a lot.
Mummy stood at the door with my bag and said we would be late for tuition. I pulled ten more times, maybe. Same thing. Nothing changed at all.
Now I am borrowing my sister's maths set, and it has a bent compass. I am still cross with the drawer. Tomorrow I will pull even harder.

qa.q: How did Tejas try to open the stuck drawer?
qa.a: Tejas pulled, then pulled harder, then put a foot on the wall and pulled with both hands.

qa.q: What was Tejas feeling at the end of the diary entry?
qa.a: Tejas felt cross with the drawer and still wanted to open it by pulling even harder.

qa.q: What different thing could Tejas try, and why?
qa.a: Tejas could lift the drawer a little or look inside to see what is stuck, since more pulling has not changed anything.

qa.q: How might Mummy see the drawer struggle?
qa.a: Mummy was waiting at the door with the bag, so may feel worried about being late and see the pulling as using up time.

grounding: A boy keeps pushing and pulling a jammed drawer harder without lifting it or checking what is stuck.
